render.prompt: Locked-off 35 mm wide side view, static camera, no push, no zoom, no pan, one single unbroken twelve-second take from this one camera only. Start exactly from the first frame and continue the same continuous take without any cut; the camera never changes position, height or angle. The meadow at golden hour with the shallow lake at the left, the long rope across the frame, the huge brown grizzly bear with real fur and mass at the water's edge on the left with the rope in its jaws hauling, and on the right end five identical figures in long grey hooded raincoats, hoods up, faces in shadow, leaning back and hauling, with the young man in the lime-green bucket hat (soft, round-shouldered, heavy-set, washed-out grey hoodie, giant black headphones round his neck, baggy black cargo shorts, long white tube socks in black slides) at the very back of the rope heaving hardest of all. One by one, a second or so apart, the coats let go of the rope, turn and walk away out of the frame at the right, none of them looking back, until only the young man is left holding it. He digs his heels in and heaves alone for a moment, then the bear backs steadily into the lake and drags him skidding along the grass on his slides, into the shallows and down into the water with a splash, hat and all. The bear stands in the shallows with the rope in its jaws and the young man surfaces beside it, still holding the rope. Sound: rope creaking, boots letting go and walking off, one long skid through grass, a splash, a low huff from the bear, birds.
